notes:
DEDUPLICATION: The pool of 128 collapsed to 96 distinct catalog entries. Roughly 30 were true duplicates of the same issue under a second lens (most flagrant: Lethal Autonomous Weapons x4, the two Degrowth and two Nuclear-deterrence pairs, the two Smartphones/youth pairs, three+ Content-Moderation items, three AI-sentience items, and parallel pairs on gain-of-function, AI-and-work, crypto, and youth gender transition). Where two source items shared a theme but cut at genuinely different altitudes I kept BOTH and cross-linked rather than merged — notably (a) open-vs-closed-ai (release of weights) vs frontier-ai-regulation (government governance); (b) privacy-vs-surveillance (broad balance) vs encryption-vs-lawful-access (the specific backdoor fight); (c) the two immigration topics (borders/restriction vs assimilation/multiculturalism), which are distinct topic-shaped debates; (d) assisted-dying (policy) vs right-to-die (principle) and treating-aging-as-disease (science) vs should-we-live-forever (ethics), reflecting the project's deliberate bio-health-vs-ethics separation of a concrete issue from its underlying value question. Each retained pair is reciprocally cross-linked so a reader can move between the concrete and the foundational framing. No candidate was dropped for failing the contestedness/topic-first/steelmannable criteria — every entry supports 2-5 genuine named positions; the only removals were duplicates.

TAXONOMY (why 9, not the generic 6): I recommend reorganizing the existing 6-category model (energy / tech / gov / econ / ethics / risk) into 9. The pool is lopsided: AI alone yields ~14 distinct topics and biomedicine/health ~17, so a single 'AI & Technology' bucket and a single 'Economic & Social' bucket would each swamp the home/category tiers while other buckets stayed thin. Three concrete changes: (1) SPLIT the old 'AI & Technology' into **AI & Machine Intelligence** (capability, alignment, governance, machine minds) and **Digital Society & Information** (speech, privacy, surveillance, money, attention, shared truth) — they share a stack but pose different questions, and several topics (content moderation, crypto, surveillance) are about society-on-the-network, not about AI. (2) CARVE OUT **Bio, Health & the Human Body** from the catch-all 'Economic & Social' — biomedicine is the second-largest cluster and has a coherent through-line (intervening in human biology, reproduction, death). (3) SPLIT the remaining 'Economic & Social' into **Economy & Work** and **Society, Culture & Identity**, which otherwise mix monetary policy with loneliness and DEI. I kept **Climate, Energy & Environment**, **Governance & Political Order**, **Ethics & Philosophy**, and **Existential & Global Catastrophic Risk** close to the originals (renamed for scope clarity). Result: nine categories each holding ~8-17 topics with a clear one-sentence scope and minimal cross-bucket ambiguity.

CROSS-CUTTING HANDLING: Many topics legitimately touch several categories; I used primary_category_slug for the home/category badge colour (the project rule: a topic shows its primary --cat-* tint) and secondary_category_slugs for genuine spillover, so e.g. lethal-autonomous-weapons is primary=governance, secondary=[ai, global-risk]; ai-future-of-work is primary=economy, secondary=[ai]; social-media-youth-mental-health is primary=society, secondary=[digital, bio-health]. This keeps each topic single-homed for discovery while preserving the dense related_slugs web that makes the atlas navigable. ICONS are stock Phosphor names (matching the project's current Topic.icon convention — bespoke per-topic icons are parked per the design memo). Suggested category↔token mapping for the existing CAT_COLORS palette: global-risk→risk, ai→tech, digital→tech(or a new token), climate-env→energy, economy→econ, governance→gov, ethics→ethics, with bio-health and society needing two new --cat-* tokens if the 9-category split is adopted (or fold society→econ and bio-health→its own) — flagged as the one implementation cost of going past six.
